messages:
maria-cs: Hey team — customer sees sporadic 403s from our API. They gave CloudFront log files but say they can’t find our request/session correlator. What exact field(s) should we ask them to pull and what minimal repro (curl/trace) do we need?

jamie-dev: Short answer: look for the edge request id and any of our forwarded headers. CloudFront has x-edge-request-id in the logs. Also check for any custom header we inject (examples: X-RD-Session, X-RD-ReqId, X-Request-Id) — those usually show up in the cs(User-Agent)/cs(Cookie) or in the x-edge-request-id column depending on how the origin/ALB forwards headers.

nate-sre: Quick checklist I send customers: 1) exact request timestamp (UTC) + endpoint path they hit, 2) client IP, 3) the raw CloudFront log lines for that minute, 4) a minimal curl that reproduces auth headers. If they can, a HAR from the browser or a tcpdump from the client helps.

maria-cs: Jamie, can you paste the grep/cut example I should give them for CloudFront logs? They’re not very ops-savvy.

jamie-dev: Yep — give them this exact, copy-paste-friendly snippet to run from the directory with the CF logs (gzipped):
```
zcat *.gz | egrep "2026-03-17T15:02|2026-03-17T15:03" | egrep -i "x-rd|request-id|edge-request-id|X-Request-Id" -n || true
```
That looks for our common header patterns in the time window. If they want a single column (edge id) they can run:
```
zcat *.gz | awk '{print $17}' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head
```
(Positions vary by log format — if they paste the header row I can point to the exact column index.)

eng_oncall_bot: incident 2026-03-17-403 created (inc#1234) — assigned to support.

nate-sre: If they prefer a GUI walkthrough: ask them to open CloudFront console -> Logging -> download logs for that distribution -> open the gz in a text editor and search for "x-edge-request-id" or "x-rd-". If the origin stripped headers, look for the ALB/NGINX logs behind the origin — there we usually emit our X-RD-* headers.

maria-cs: For repro, what curl should I request? They said they have a simple server making the calls.

jamie-dev: Minimal curl to include: auth header, content-type, and enable verbose trace so we capture response headers. Ask them to replace the token and endpoint: 
```
curl -v -X POST 'https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-RD-Debug: capture" \
  -d '{"input":"hello"}' --trace-ascii ./curl-trace.txt
```
Then have them attach curl-trace.txt plus the CloudFront log lines for the same timestamp. The trace file shows request/response headers we can match against the log.

nate-sre: Also ask them to include the exact response body for the 403 (copy/paste, not screenshot). 403s often include an error message and an internal code that we use to tie into our backend logs.

maria-cs: Good. Any easy way for non-technical PMs to capture the header from a webview (mobile) or embedded browser?

jamie-dev: For webview/mobile: 1) If they can reproduce on desktop, use Chrome DevTools -> Network -> click the failing request -> Headers -> look for X-RD-*. 2) If mobile webview only, ask for a screen recording showing DevTools-like network if they have it, or ask them to enable our SDK debug flag (if using web/mobile SDK) which prints the session id to console/logcat. Example SDK config snippet they can add: 
```js
Redwood.init({ debug: true, onDebug: console.log })
// SDK prints: "rd_session: abc123"
```
If they send that printed token + CloudFront lines for the same minute we can correlate.

maria-cs: Perfect. Anything else to request to speed escalation to eng?

nate-sre: Yep — include the following in the initial escalation bundle: 1) curl-trace.txt (or HAR), 2) CloudFront log snippet (raw lines), 3) the application timestamp and timezone, 4) client IP, 5) full response body for 403, 6) which model/route they called. Zip and upload to the secure ticket or paste a short S3 link.

maria-cs: I’ll send the customer this step-by-step and ask them to run the two commands + curl. Thanks! :thumbsup:

jamie-dev: Happy to jump on the ticket if they paste the raw logs. If they paste the header row from one gz I’ll point to exact column numbers.

nate-sre: If we can’t find the header in CF logs we’ll ask ops to check the origin (ALB/NGINX) — sometimes headers are stripped by a CDN rule.

maria-cs: Upload incoming in ~30m, will ping here once done.
thread_summary: Support rep requests guidance for extracting request/session correlator from CloudFront logs and a minimal curl repro to correlate 403s. Engineers provide grep/awk snippets, a curl trace example, and a checklist of what to attach for escalation.
